title: Without Food, Bigger People Last Longer 🏝️
short_title: Without Food, Bigger People Last Longer 🏝️
title_options: Without Food, Bigger People Last Longer 🏝️
One Man Didn't Eat for 382 Days 😳
Body Fat Is Your Backup Food Tank 😳
seo_intro:
How long can you survive without food? With water, a bigger person usually lasts longer: a lean man has about 20 pounds of body fat (roughly two months), a big man can have 100 pounds (many months).
Body fat holds about 3,500 calories per pound, but the body also burns muscle, even the heart. Angus Barbieri fasted 382 days under medical supervision in Scotland (1965–66) and lost 276 pounds.
sources_text: Leiter L.A. & Marliss E.B., "Survival during fasting may depend on fat as well as protein stores", JAMA, 1982 (1981 hunger strikers died after about two months, when fat stores ran out); Stewart W.K. & Fleming L.W., "Features of a successful therapeutic fast of 382 days' duration", Postgraduate Medical Journal, 1973 (Angus Barbieri, Dundee, 1965–66: 456 to 180 lb); Cahill G.F., "Starvation in man", New England Journal of Medicine, 1970 (fat and protein fuel stores during starvation); Keys A. et al., The Biology of Human Starvation (Minnesota Starvation Experiment), 1950 (loss of muscle mass and heart size); Wishnofsky M., "Caloric equivalents of gained or lost weight", American Journal of Clinical Nutrition, 1958 (about 3,500 calories per pound of body fat, an approximation). Figures for the two men are rounded illustrations.
disclaimer: Original illustrations (simplified). Synthetic voice and AI-generated music. Not medical advice: never fast without a doctor.
